cluster: Commit-on-Next overloads 'Next' and keeps no draft ledger
title: Picking a cloud provider with no key traps Next and mouse users; only Enter-in-field skips
problem: After choosing a keyed provider with an empty key, Next/Ctrl+N shows the pinned red strip 'API key required. Set OPENAI_API_KEY or add api_key under [api_settings.openai].  Retry with Next, or go Back.' Retrying yields the same refusal every time; 'go Back' goes to Welcome. There is no Skip control and the list cannot be unselected. The only way past is Enter inside the empty password field (skip_without_key), mentioned only at the end of the small help line: 'No key yet? Enter skips this step — you can add a provider later in Settings.' Welcome promised 'most steps can be skipped with Next', and the footer says 'Enter / Ctrl+N next', implying Enter and Ctrl+N are the same action. In the mouse-only run, two clicks on Next changed nothing.
impact: First-time (no key yet, or exploring): stuck on step 2 and told to edit environment variables or a TOML table; mouse users must abandon the provider choice or exit setup. Power user: learns an undocumented exception to 'Next skips'. Violates H3 User control and freedom (no visible skip/emergency exit), H9 Help users recognize, diagnose and recover from errors (the suggested remedy 'Retry with Next' can never succeed), H4 Consistency and standards (Next skips on every other step; Enter and Ctrl+N advertised as equivalent but differ), H7 Flexibility (escape is keyboard-only).
correction: none. Small additions: Back leads to Welcome, and Next from there lands on the same refusal. The refusal strip is also never cleared when the provider changes: after switching OpenAI→Anthropic it still read 'Set OPENAI_API_KEY … [api_settings.openai]' (cross-cutting-07 covers stale strips).

cluster: Highlight drives selection and focused widgets swallow Enter
title: Detected local server gets lost: Enter picks OpenAI, a manual pick ignores the found port
problem: Auto-detect shows 'Found a local endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:9099.' with a 'Use this server' button, but focus stays in the provider list with OpenAI highlighted. Pressing Enter selects OpenAI: the banner and button vanish and are replaced by 'Couldn't discover models for OpenAI. Set OPENAI_API_KEY or add api_key under [api_settings.openai]. Or go Back.' and an expanded API key field. Clicking llama.cpp afterwards fills Endpoint 'http://localhost:8080' (Chat URL …:8080) with 'Couldn't discover models for llama.cpp. You can continue anyway.' — the server found seconds earlier is forgotten until the user presses 'Find local servers' and picks the detected row. 'Use this server' is reachable only by Shift+Tab or mouse; the code comment says it is 'only reachable backwards or by click'.
impact: First-time local user (Jo): loses the found server with one keystroke and is pushed toward a cloud key; picking the right engine still fails. Keyboard power user: the primary local CTA is outside the Tab order. Violates H1 Visibility of system status (detection result silently discarded), H5 Error prevention (default focus makes the wrong choice one keystroke away), H6 Recognition rather than recall (must remember 'Find local servers' / Shift+Tab), H7 Flexibility (no accelerator for the primary action).
correction: Enter selecting the highlighted OpenAI row is normal OptionList behaviour, and the User Guide documents it, so on its own it is weak evidence. The stronger defect is that ANY provider pick drops the detection. Clicking llama.cpp directly while the banner says 'Found a local endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:9099.' (no Enter misstep) clears the banner, fills Endpoint 'http://localhost:8080' and shows 'Couldn't discover models for llama.cpp. You can continue anyway.' Tab from the list goes to '← Back' (verified by ANSI focus style), so 'Use this server' is only reachable with Shift+Tab or a click. Contamination note: a foreign Next.js server listens on *:8080. On a clean machine :8080 would be connection-refused, not HTML; the outcome (discovery fails) is the same.

root_cause: (1) preferred_focus() always returns #setup-provider-choice (FRW:1440-1450), and the auto-discovery result is applied via _apply_discovered_server, which highlights the row only in the hidden Detected-endpoints list (FRW:1759-1782), so the provider list's initial highlight stays on OpenAI and Enter on an OptionList means Select. (2) select_provider() calls _clear_detected_provider_state() on every provider change (FRW:2862-2864), hiding the banner and forgetting _detected_servers. (3) _initial_endpoint_for() (FRW:2260-2280) prefers the template's configured endpoint (llama_cpp api_url = http://localhost:8080) over a server just detected. (4) The Use button precedes the list in visual order, so Tab from the list skips it.
solution: Let detection drive the default. When discovery finds a server and nothing is selected: move the provider-list highlight to the detected engine's row and return the 'Use this server' button from preferred_focus(), so Enter means 'use it'; relabel the button with the engine ('Use llama.cpp on this computer'). Keep detection sticky: _clear_detected_provider_state() should only hide the banner while a non-matching provider is selected, and restore banner and button when the user returns to a matching provider or to no selection; never drop _detected_servers on a switch. Make _initial_endpoint_for() prefer a detected server for that provider and say so: '✓ Using the llama.cpp server found at http://127.0.0.1:9099 — 3 models.' While the banner shows, add a visible accelerator to the hint line ('u use found server') so the button is reachable without Shift+Tab. Also removes the duplicate-affordance clutter in provider-09.
solution_review: Sticky detection, and making _initial_endpoint_for prefer a detected server for that engine, are the core, low-risk fixes. Do them first. Moving focus to the 'Use this server' button above the list fights the established Tab order (TASK-1496). A cleaner pattern: render the detection as the first row of the provider list ('llama.cpp on this computer · 127.0.0.1:9099 · 3 models'), pre-highlighted, so Enter means 'use it' and the arrows still browse. That also removes the separate button and the duplicate-affordance clutter. Skip the 'u' accelerator; it adds a one-off binding the footer has to explain.

cluster: Status indicators not grounded in verified, in-effect state
title: Provider step ignores its own failed checks: refused or rejected setups advance with ✓
problem: After the step reports '✗ The connection was refused - nothing is listening at that address. Start the server, or check the endpoint and port.', Next advances with no question and the tracker shows a green ✓ for Provider for the whole Model step; it flips to '!' only after the Model step's 'Continue anyway?'. With a mistyped Anthropic key, Next advances, Provider turns green ✓, and the rejection appears only on Model as a dim, disabled-looking radio row: 'Authentication failed — this API key was rejected. Go Back to fix it, or enter a model ID below.' The second clause invites continuing with a rejected key. Back then shows 'Couldn't discover models for Anthropic. You can continue anyway.' beside the red 'The last connection check failed: this API key was rejected. Update it, then continue.'
impact: First-time: the tracker says the provider is done when it is not; the error lands on the next step looking like a disabled option, and the copy offers a way to continue into a broken first chat. Power user: the wizard has a confirmation gate, but on the wrong step. Violates H1 Visibility of system status (✓ for a failed connection), H5 Error prevention (no gate where the failure is known), H9 (error shown away from its cause, with an option to proceed), H4 Consistency (Model asks 'Continue anyway?', Provider does not).
correction: The 'silent wrong outcome' framing is overstated. Model shows 'Couldn't reach the server (connection refused)…' and 'Authentication failed — this API key was rejected…' immediately. Next then raises 'Continue anyway? / The API key failed an authentication check, so this model setup is unverified.' [Keep editing] [Continue anyway]. The ✓ on Provider is premature, and the contradictory pairs on Back are real: 'Couldn't discover models for Custom OpenAI-compatible. You can continue anyway.' next to the red 'The last connection check couldn't reach the server. Check it's running, then continue.'

root_cause: ProviderStep.commit (FRW:3248-3290) gates only on readiness (credential/endpoint present) and staging. It never consults the step's own ProviderTestEvidenceStore (_provider_test_evidence) or the outcome of the selected-provider discovery it already started (it restarts it if stale, FRW:3276-3280), so a known 'unreachable' or 'unauthorized' outcome affects neither Next nor the tracker. Attention ('!') is derived from the Model step's probe failure (FRW:9359-9378), so Provider stays ✓ until then.
solution: Put the trust gate where the fault is. In ProviderStep.commit: (1) if the latest evidence or discovery for this exact draft identity is unauthorized/forbidden, refuse with a field-level error under the key: '✗ Anthropic rejected this key. Check it was copied completely, or paste a new one.' — no 'continue' wording; (2) if it is unreachable or an invalid response, push the same safe-default confirm the Model step uses ('Couldn't reach http://127.0.0.1:18699. Continue without a working connection?' [Keep editing] [Continue anyway]) and, on continue, set Provider attention '!' immediately; (3) if discovery for a keyed provider is still running, make the Next busy state read 'Checking your key…' and await _selected_discovery_done (bounded by the existing 8 s timeout); on timeout continue with '!' rather than ✓. Remove 'or enter a model ID below' from the Model-step auth-failure row (TASK-33008.5). Publish the settled outcome to the shared evidence owner (TASK-33005.9) so Summary and Console agree.
solution_review: Part (1) is right: refuse on a definitive unauthorized/forbidden outcome, with a field-level error. Part (2), a second 'Continue anyway?' on Provider for unreachable servers, duplicates the Model-step gate and causes confirm fatigue. 'Set it up now, start the server later' is a legitimate local path. Instead, set Provider attention '!' as soon as a failed outcome for the committed draft is known, and keep a single gate. Part (3), blocking Next for up to 8 s on every keyed Next, adds latency to the happy path. Prefer advancing at once and letting the tracker flip to '!' when the in-flight discovery settles. Dropping 'or enter a model ID below' from the auth row is correct.

root_cause: resolve_provider_endpoint prefixes 'http://' when '://' is absent (provider_endpoint_contract.py:178-179), so 'htp:/foo' parses with netloc 'htp:' and hits the empty-port branch. Probe failures map to fixed category strings without the status code or TLS-mismatch detection; a 404 on the models route of a reachable host maps to a neutral 'unavailable' verdict; commit's invalid-draft refusal is generic.
solution: Before prefixing, detect scheme typos (':/' without '//', or an unknown scheme before ':') → 'Start the address with http:// or https:// (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8080).' Under a disabled Test button show the reason: 'Fix the endpoint above to enable Test connection.' Commit refusal names the field: 'The endpoint isn't a valid address — fix it above or pick another provider.' In provider_test_evidence: TLS wrong-version errors → 'This server speaks plain HTTP — try http:// instead of https://.'; a 404 on the models route of a host that answered → '! The server answered, but there's no model list at /api/v1/models — remove /api from the endpoint?' (a warning, not neutral); include the code: 'HTTP 500 — the server hit an internal error; check its logs.' Settings shares the evidence module and benefits too.
solution_review: Good. Keep the 404 case non-blocking, given the deliberate design, and add the 'remove /api?' hint only when the path has extra segments beyond a recognized suffix. Including the HTTP status code is trivial and high value.

cluster: Commit-on-Next overloads 'Next' and keeps no draft ledger
title: Next/Enter on Model without a pick silently throws away the provider and key just entered
problem: The Provider step only stages the connection in memory. The provider, key and endpoint are written only when the Model step commits a model. With no row pressed, Next/Enter on Model returns 'skip-safe' and writes nothing, so the staged key is dropped. The UI never says so: the tracker keeps Provider ✓ and gives Model an unexplained amber '!'. The Summary then blames the user with '✗ Provider — no credentials or saved endpoint', although they had entered credentials. Protect still offers 'Set a password' for a key that was never saved. On the server-down path the only warning is 'Continue anyway? / The server couldn't be reached, so this model setup is unverified. Continue anyway?'. It does not say that continuing without a model saves nothing. Nothing is preselected, not even the '(recommended)' row. Enter on a freshly rendered list does not select the highlighted row either, because no row is highlighted yet.
impact: First-time (Sam, Jo): believes setup succeeded, lands in Console with chat blocked and the key gone. The draft scrubs secrets, so Resume cannot restore it, and the key must be found and pasted again. Privacy-minded local user: an explicit local choice is replaced by a leftover cloud default, and Home's 'Set up Console model' opens Settings preset to OpenAI. Power-user: the same trap whenever they accept the visible recommendation with Enter. Heuristics: H1 visibility of system status (✓ on Provider while nothing is saved; '!' with no text); H5 error prevention (the default key leads to a destructive outcome); H9 help users recover (the Summary misattributes the cause); H3 user control (no undo, and the loss is invisible).
correction: The core claim holds, but the impact narrative is partly wrong. (1) The user is not 'landed in Console believing setup succeeded'. With this state the Summary hides 'Start chatting', and its focused primary is 'Review provider setup' (FRW:7826-7835). (2) The key is not lost at the Model step. It stays staged in memory: after 'Review provider setup' the Provider step still showed the masked key and 'Found 13 model(s) for Anthropic.' It is lost only when the wizard is exited (Explore Home, Add your first document, Write your first note, Review settings, Esc, or a quit), because the checkpoint scrubs secrets. (3) The more serious recovery defect is not mentioned. 'Review provider setup' routes to Provider, not Model, and nothing says a model is missing. Ctrl+N then re-renders the same untouched list, and Enter drops the pair again (loop reproduced, capture 06). Line refs are accurate: skip-safe at FRW:4198, `_selected = None` at FRW:3792, the bail-out at FRW:239.

Constraint: task-25820 (Done, closed INVALID): pre-pressing index 0 was tried and reverted because the step is deliberately skip-safe (34 pinning tests). task-25818 (Done) added the '!' marker.
root_cause: Two specs collide. The 08-12 atomic provider+model write moved provider persistence into ModelStep.commit (FRW:4199). The older 'skip-safe' rule returns (True, '') when no model is chosen (FRW:4196-4198), so the staged draft is dropped. _render_models sets radio_set._selected = None after every render (FRW:3792), so SetupRadioSet._select_highlighted bails at FRW:239 and Enter advances with nothing pressed. ModelStep.confirm_before_advance (FRW:3393-3407) only fires for PROVIDER_PROBE_AUTH/CONNECTION. The tracker's setup_attention_ids keys on wizard_data provider_key (in memory), not on persisted state (STATE:1329-1334).
solution: Fix the collision explicitly, without silently auto-committing a model (this respects task-25820's ruling). (1) After _render_models mounts real rows, seat the highlight, not the press, on the recommended or current row (radio_set._selected = idx). Enter on the focused list then presses that visible row through the existing _select_highlighted: one deliberate keystroke accepts the recommendation. (2) Extend ModelStep.confirm_before_advance with a dedicated three-way dialog whenever a provider is staged and no model is chosen. Title: 'No model chosen'. Body: 'Anthropic won't be saved without a default model — the API key you entered will be discarded.' For local providers: '…the llama.cpp server address you entered won't be saved.' Buttons: primary 'Use claude-sonnet-5-5 (recommended)' commits the pair; 'Choose a model' has default focus and returns to the list; 'Skip — don't save Anthropic'. When there is no recommendation (server down or empty list), the primary becomes 'Type a model ID' and focuses the input. (3) Tracker: while the provider is only staged, Provider renders a neutral 'staged' mark, not ✓. After a skip it renders '!'. Whenever a step shows '!', a one-line caption under the tracker names why: 'Model not chosen — Anthropic wasn't saved'. (4) Summary: for this state replace '✗ Provider — no credentials or saved endpoint' with '✗ Provider — Anthropic wasn't saved because no model was chosen' and make 'Choose a model' the primary action (reusing the Review-provider-setup route with the staged draft). Protect hides 'Set a password' when no key will be written (cross-area). (5) User Guide skip paragraph: 'Skipping the Model step also discards the provider you just entered.' (6) Regression tests: test-then-skip shows the dialog and writes nothing; Enter on a fresh list commits the recommended pair; the existing skip-safe pins are rewritten on purpose. Optional owner call: support a provider-only save (api_settings without chat_defaults) so 'Skip' keeps the key. The same fix removes the unexplained '!' (cloud-35) and the leftover cloud default after a local choice (local-04).
solution_review:
Direction is right, but the order and one sub-fix need changing. (a) The root fix should be the 'optional owner call', not an afterthought. When Model is skipped, persist the staged credential and endpoint into api_settings.

without touching chat_defaults. The 08-12 atomic write protects the consistency of the chat_defaults (provider, model) pair; a credential-only write does not break that. Skip-safe would then mean 'don't change my default model' rather than 'discard what I typed', and the P0 data loss disappears whatever the user presses. (b) Keep the confirm on Next, but as the existing two-button _SettlingGuardedConfirmationDialog: 'Choose a model' (default focus) and 'Skip — keep the key, no default model'. A third 'Use ' button must wait for model-02's ranking. Today it would offer tts-1-hd-1106 as a one-click primary in a large share of OpenAI runs. (c) Item (1), seating the highlight on the recommended row, has the same model-02 dependency. One Down already selects row 0 (verified), so its main gain is a visible cursor. (d) 'Review provider setup' should land on Model (or open the dialog) when the provider is staged and only the model is missing. Otherwise the loop remains. (e) For the tracker, prefer flagging Provider '!' when the staged draft was not persisted, and put the reason in the existing step-error line above the nav. That avoids a fourth glyph state. Summary copy (4) and the guide line (5) are good. File this under task-26837 (its description is this exact symptom) and rewrite the task-25820 pins on purpose.

cluster: No end-to-end 'first chat works' contract across Summary and handoff
title: '(recommended)' is just the API's first id: often a TTS/realtime model, different each run
problem: The '(recommended)' tag goes on whatever id the discovery endpoint returned first. Nothing is curated, filtered or sorted. OpenAI's /v1/models order is not stable, so four fresh runs recommended four different models, one of them a text-to-speech model. 10 of the 20 OpenAI rows cannot chat at all (tts-1, gpt-realtime-*, gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize, omni-moderation, gpt-image-1-mini, gpt-audio-1.5, sora-2, babbage-002). On Ollama, embedding models such as 'nomic-embed-text:latest' are offered as chat defaults. The wizard accepts any of them and the Summary ticks it ('✓ Default model — tts-1-hd-1106').
impact: First-time: reads 'recommended' as the app's evaluated advice, picks a speech model, and the first message fails with a jargon block ('This request cannot fit the selected model…'). Trust in every later recommendation drops. Power-user: noisy, unordered list. Advice that changes per run reads as broken. Heuristics: H2 match between system and real world ('recommended' implies judgement); H5 error prevention (non-chat models offered as chat defaults); H4 consistency (a different recommendation each run); H8 minimalist design (half the rows are irrelevant).
correction: (1) The order is not random per call. OpenAI serves a few distinct orderings: 4 distinct heads in 8 calls, each repeated. The `created` fields in those heads are unsorted, which falsifies the FRW:1002-1005 comment ('roughly chronological'). That comment should be removed, because the [:20] slice was justified by it. (2) When the recommended row happens to be a chat model, the first chat works: o3-2025-04-16 was recommended, picked and sent, and the reply was 'hello there'. So the harm is probabilistic, though frequent. (3) OpenRouter's order is newest-first and stable, so its '(recommended)' row (inclusionai/ling-3.1-flash) is arbitrary but not unstable, and 451 of 466 entries carry text-only output_modalities. (4) The Ollama 'nomic-embed-text:latest' observation came from the QA fake server's fixture, not a real Ollama. The risk is real, but that evidence is synthetic.

cluster: Commit-on-Next overloads 'Next' and keeps no draft ledger
title: Next on an untouched Voice step writes TTS config and overwrites a working setup on re-run
problem: The subtitle reads "Hear replies read aloud — optional. PocketTTS or OmniVoice run locally, no account needed; skip with Next if you don't want voice." Next always saves instead. In every live profile that passed Voice untouched (local1-6, res1/2/3/5/6, cloud2, power2), Next wrote [app_tts] OPENAI_BASE_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:8765/v1/audio/speech", OPENAI_AUTH_MODE = "none", default_provider = "openai", default_model = "tts-1-hd", default_voice = "shimmer", default_format = "mp3", and duplicated these into [tts_settings]. Only profiles that never reached Voice (local2b, res4, probe) have no [app_tts]. With 'Use as default' unticked, the PocketTTS preset's own model, voice and format (pocket-tts / alba / wav) are dropped, and runtime fallbacks are written as the default. The result points the OpenAI TTS backend at the PocketTTS port with OpenAI voice names. On a re-run, Next changed OPENAI_BASE_URL from https://api.openai.com/v1/audio/speech to the loopback PocketTTS URL and changed OPENAI_AUTH_MODE from api_key to none, keeping tts-1-hd/shimmer. This reproduced twice, and Exit setup did not roll it back.
impact: First-time: a user who skipped voice now has a default TTS provider that cannot speak. The first 'Speak replies' fails, with nothing linking the failure to the wizard. Power user: re-running setup to change one thing silently breaks a working OpenAI TTS setup, with no undo, and the prior endpoint is lost. Heuristics: #1 Visibility of system status (silent write), #3 User control and freedom (no real skip, no undo), #4 Consistency and standards (the copy says skip; untouched Speech and Tools steps write nothing), #5 Error prevention.
correction: The first-run harm is described wrongly in both directions. (a) Overstated for keyless users. With no [app_tts], the effective TTS default was already openai/tts-1-hd/shimmer against https://api.openai.com/v1/audio/speech with API-key auth (TTS/backends/openai.py:31,67-71; openai_compatible_config.py:200-212). A keyless user could not hear speech before the step either, so nothing that worked is lost; what they gain is a false '✓ Voice — PocketTTS (default voice)' and a Console 'Ready · not tested'. (b) Understated for users who do have an OpenAI key, e.g. a cloud user who picked OpenAI on Provider. Before the step, TTS worked through the official endpoint plus get_api_key('openai'). An untouched Next redirects it to 127.0.0.1:8765 with auth none, which breaks working TTS on the FIRST run, not only on re-run. The rest holds as written: the hybrid table, the PocketTTS model/voice/format dropped in favour of tts-1-hd/shimmer/mp3, no rollback on Exit, and the duplicate [tts_settings]. Also verified that this contradicts TASK-32959 AC#2: Summary showed '✓ Voice — PocketTTS (default voice)' after an untouched Next with 'Use as default' unticked.

root_cause: VoiceSetupStep._initial_draft() (FRW:4295-4305) always builds the PocketTTS draft, and no code reads [app_tts]. commit() (FRW:5127-5165) has no untouched/delta check and always posts build_voice_setup_save_event(), which always includes OPENAI_BASE_URL and OPENAI_AUTH_MODE (first_run_voice_step_state.py:201-238). When use_as_default is False, the event's preferences are None. Because commit_defaults_after_handoff is also False, the STTS handler builds TTSPreferencesSnapshot.from_settings() from the current effective settings and writes it as the defaults (stts_events.py:2028-2040). That is why default_provider/model/voice/format appear even with the box unticked. The only path that writes nothing is the hidden OmniVoice + unticked combination (FRW:5169-5171).
solution: One root-cause fix in three parts. It also clears voice-speech-02's false check mark, static-code-map-38's resume-as-Custom and the User Guide's skipped-voice drift. (1) Skip option: make the first Service radio 'No voice for now' (id setup-voice-preset-none), preselected on a first run when the raw [app_tts] table is absent. Choosing it hides sample, test, default and Advanced and shows 'Nothing is saved. Set up a voice any time in Settings > Speech & TTS.' commit() then returns (True, '') and posts nothing. (2) Re-run prefill: add a pure voice_draft_from_config(raw_app_tts) to first_run_voice_step_state.py. It maps OPENAI_BASE_URL to the PocketTTS, OpenAI or Custom preset (default_provider 'omnivoice' maps to OmniVoice) and fills model, voice, format and speed from default_*. It ticks 'Use as default' when the saved default matches, and the step shows 'Current voice: OpenAI · tts-1-hd · shimmer — unchanged unless you edit it.' (3) Delta commit: add should_persist_voice_config(draft, persisted, acted_this_run), mirroring should_persist_speech_config. Write only when the draft differs from what is saved, or when the user tested or ticked default this run. A save with 'Use as default' unticked passes a new STTSSettingsSaveEvent flag (e.g. persist_default_preferences=False) so that _persist_settings skips preference_mutation. A preset's model, voice and format are always written together with its endpoint, so a PocketTTS URL is never paired with tts-1-hd/shimmer/mp3. New subtitle: 'Hear replies read aloud — optional. Pick a service to try it, or keep "No voice for now" — nothing is saved unless you choose one.' Replace the pinning test with one asserting that an untouched commit posts nothing. Add a test that Next through Voice on a populated config leaves [app_tts] and [tts_settings] byte-identical, and fix First_Run_Setup.md.
solution_review: Sound, and it fixes the root cause. Three notes. (1) Ship order: the smallest safe slice is the delta/untouched gate, i.e. commit() posts nothing when the draft equals what is saved (or equals the initial draft on a profile with no raw [app_tts]) and the user neither tested nor ticked default. That slice alone stops the clobbering. 'No voice for now' and the re-run prefill are the right follow-ups for clarity. (2) The prefill must read the RAW [app_tts] from COMPREHENSIVE_CONFIG_RAW or load_cli_config_and_ensure_existence. It must not read a top-level app_config key: load_settings() has no top-level 'transcription', and the Speech step already fell into exactly that trap (see the new issue). (3) The proposed persist_default_preferences=False flag is needed. Without it, the STTS handler's from_settings() snapshot keeps materializing default_provider='openai', and that is what turns the Summary into the false '(default voice)'. Replacing the pinning test test_voice_save_waits_for_applied_runtime_when_default_is_opted_out is correct. Also add a re-run test with a custom endpoint and a first-run test with an OpenAI key present (the case this report adds).

cluster: Shipped template values masquerade as user choices
title: Preselected PocketTTS needs a server that isn't running; test fails with no cause or fix
problem: The subtitle promises "PocketTTS or OmniVoice run locally, no account needed", and PocketTTS is preselected. 'Test and Hear' fails at once with "Not tested yet — the sample failed. Check the service, then retry." (three independent live runs: cloud, power-user, resilience). Nothing on the step explains that PocketTTS is a separate server that must be installed and running on 127.0.0.1:8765, or how to start it. Nothing suggests OpenAI either: it is not preselected even when OPENAI_API_KEY is in the environment or the user has just entered an OpenAI key on the Provider step. OmniVoice, the other 'runs locally' option, needs `pip install "tldw_chatbook[omnivoice_tts]"` plus a 1.1 GB download (code only; no live run chose it).
impact: First-time local-first user: the promised local option fails on the first try, and the copy contradicts itself ('not tested' vs 'failed'), so users conclude voice is broken. Power user: wastes a test before switching to OpenAI by hand. Heuristics: #9 Help users recognize, diagnose and recover from errors; #2 Match between system and real world ('runs locally' implies it ships with the app); #1 Visibility of system status; #10 Help and documentation.
correction: The contamination statement in verify_hint is false. 127.0.0.1:8765 has been held since 2026-09-29 20:18 by another session's schema_proxy.py (PID 60473). That proxy answers /v1/audio/speech with HTTP 404 {"error":"unknown route"}. So the three original live failures were 404s from a stray proxy, not a refused connection. The user-facing copy is identical either way, because _run_voice_sample has a bare except at FRW:4967-4974. I reproduced the genuine not-running case on an empty port in my range (127.0.0.1:19399) and got the same 'Not tested yet — the sample failed. Check the service, then retry.' The failure also came back in under 0.3 s, so a probe is cheap. Side finding: on this machine, any wizard run that keeps the PocketTTS preset talks to a different session's proxy.
evidence: evidence/verify-voice-speech/14-voice-pocket-testing-immediate.txt (failure string already shown at +0.3 s, against the contaminating 404)

root_cause: The PocketTTS preset is hard-coded as the default (FRW:4273-4275), and the step never probes whether it is reachable. _run_voice_sample turns every exception into one string (FRW:4967-4974), throwing away httpx.ConnectError and HTTP status. Preselection ignores _existing_openai_credential() (FRW:4915-4955).
solution: (1) When the step shows and when the preset changes, run a worker probe of at most 1 s: TCP connect to 127.0.0.1:8765, check _existing_openai_credential(), and reuse the OmniVoice state check that already exists. Add each result to its radio label: 'PocketTTS — not running on this computer', 'OpenAI — uses your OpenAI key', 'OmniVoice — one-time 1.1 GB download'. (2) Preselect the saved config first (voice-speech-01), otherwise 'No voice for now'. Mark OpenAI '(key found)' when a key exists, and never preselect a service whose probe failed. (3) Classify failures in run_voice_sample/_run_voice_sample. Loopback ConnectError: 'Couldn't reach PocketTTS at 127.0.0.1:8765 — it isn't running. PocketTTS is a separate local server; start it (see the User Guide's Voice section), or choose OpenAI or OmniVoice.' 401/403: 'The speech server rejected the API key.' 404: 'No speech endpoint at <host> — check Endpoint under Advanced.' Timeout: 'The speech server didn't answer within 20 seconds.' Non-audio body: 'The server answered, but not with audio.' Start each with 'Test failed —' instead of 'Not tested yet —'. (4) New subtitle: 'Hear replies read aloud — optional. OpenAI uses your OpenAI key; OmniVoice runs on this computer after a one-time 1.1 GB download; PocketTTS needs its own local server running.'
solution_review: Good. Classified errors are the core fix. Preselecting 'No voice for now' (voice-speech-01), or the saved config, removes most of the pain without any probe. If a probe is added, keep it to a single connect with a timeout under 1 s, run it in a worker, and never let it block the step. The radio-label suffixes are nice but must not reflow the 4-up segmented row at 120 cols; a status line under the radio would be safer. 'Test failed —' instead of 'Not tested yet —' is correct.

root_cause: _refresh_sample_state disables #setup-voice-test while _test_in_progress_generation is set (FRW:4809-4813), and nothing restores focus afterwards. Textual Input defaults to select_on_focus=True. validate_voice_setup_draft checks the sample text as part of the save path. The wizard-level Input.Submitted handler turns Enter into Next.
solution: Keep 'Test and Hear' enabled during a test and relabel it 'Testing… (press to cancel)' so focus never drops. Otherwise, remember app.focused before disabling and call query_one('#setup-voice-test').focus() in the test's finally block. Build the sample Input with select_on_focus=False. Validate the sample only on the test path; commit() falls back to the default sample when the field is blank. solution_review: Do these three: restore focus to #setup-voice-test in the finally block (remembering the prior focus), set select_on_focus=False on the sample, and stop validating the sample in commit(), falling back to the default text. Be careful with 'Enter in Sample text = Test'. The wizard-wide convention (UAT N-1 / TASK-21142) is that Enter in an Input advances, so an exception on one field must be signposted in the hint line, as proposed, or it becomes a new inconsistency. Keeping the button enabled as 'Testing… (press to cancel)' is fine but adds cancel semantics; the focus-restore is simpler.

title: Voice copy polish: phantom Save, unexplained 'Use as default', wrong-tense success line
problem: The default status "Not tested yet — that's fine. You can save now and test later." refers to a Save button that does not exist (Next saves). 'Use as default' never says what it is a default for, and it stays unticked even after a successful test. "Verified. The sample is ready to hear." appears after the sample has already played (it is set only when played=True). The failure line "Not tested yet — the sample failed." contradicts itself. 'Test and Hear' uses the same primary blue as Next. Under Advanced, Voice is free text ('shimmer') with no list, Format is free text, and 'Authentication: API key' does not say which key it uses. The Summary 'Voice — OpenAI (default voice)' leaves out model and voice.
impact: Small costs that add up on a step newcomers already treat as optional, and two primary buttons compete for attention. Heuristics: #2 Match between system and real world, #4 Consistency and standards, #6 Recognition rather than recall (free-text voice and format), #8 Aesthetic and minimalist design.
correction: 'Verified. The sample is ready to hear.' does not appear after the sample has played. It appears as playback STARTS: AsyncAudioPlayer.play runs the sync player in an executor, and that player spawns the OS player with subprocess.Popen and returns without waiting (TTS/audio_player.py:298-410, 771-775). The tense is still wrong ('ready to hear' while it is already playing). Two primaries confirmed: Test and Hear is variant='primary', and Next is switched to 'primary' at runtime (BaseWizard.py:254). The other items are confirmed as written.

title: Parallel OmniVoice and Parakeet installs are untested; total download size is never shown
problem: Neither install blocks Next, because both run on background workers. A Full-track user can therefore run about 1.7 GB of downloads at once into the same managed artifact store. Per-artifact locks are expected to keep them apart, but no test or live run has exercised this (TASK-33079). Nothing shows the combined size against the Welcome promise 'Quick takes about 2 minutes; Full about 10'.
impact: Power user: risk of a failed or corrupted install, bandwidth contention, and an unexpectedly long setup with no combined progress. Heuristics: #1 Visibility of system status, #5 Error prevention.
correction: The premise that the two installs run in parallel, with about 1.7 GB downloading at once and a corruption risk held off only by per-artifact locks, does not match the code. provision() holds ONE global exclusive session lease (ACQUISITION_SESSION_LEASE_KEY '#managed-acquisition/session/global', non-blocking, 0.1 s timeout; acquisition.py:1179-1205) for the whole download. OmniVoice (managed_service()) and Parakeet (parakeet_v2_managed_service()) use the same managed store. I checked that a second thread in the same process cannot take that lease (ArtifactLeaseTimeoutError), and provision maps that to AcquisitionBusyError. So the second install most likely fails fast with install_failure_message's 'Another {model_label} install is already in progress. Try again shortly.'. That copy names the wrong model: starting Parakeet while OmniVoice downloads would say 'Another Parakeet v2 (English, INT8) install is already in progress'. TASK-33079 is still To Do with all ACs unchecked, so this remains untested end to end.
tracked_task: task-33079 (To Do)
root_cause: Each step owns its own install worker, there is no shared download coordinator, and no test covers concurrent provisioning of two artifacts.
solution: Do TASK-33079 (fake-source concurrent provisioning test, plus a live run). Show in-flight downloads on the tracker ('Voice ↓34%', 'Speech ↓12%') and on Summary ('Downloads in progress: 2 — 1.1 GB + 633 MiB'). Route both through the download job owner proposed in voice-speech-10.
solution_review: Doing TASK-33079 is right, but its premise should be updated to: concurrent installs serialize via the session lease, so the second one fails as busy. The near-term fix is to queue the second install, e.g. through the shared job owner proposed in voice-speech-10 with 'Waiting for the voice model download to finish…', or at least to make the busy copy name the other download. Showing the combined size on the tracker and Summary is a nice addition, not the fix.

When it is not (e.g. faster-whisper absent on Linux), dictation falls back to parakeet-onnx and does use the download, with a 'Configured dictation provider ... isn't available' warning. title: An interrupted speech download leaves an orphaned partial file and restarts from zero
problem: After relaunch the Speech step says "Not installed." and does not mention the interrupted download. The install review reports "Already staged: 0.0 MiB", while models/managed/staging/download-09a5…/payload/encoder-model.int8.onnx holds a partial file (reported as 129 MiB; it is 120,586,240 bytes in homes/res6 today). impact: A user who retries pays for the download twice, and orphaned files build up unseen. Heuristics: #9 Help users recognize, diagnose and recover from errors, #1 Visibility of system status.
correction: Two parts are overstated. (1) 'Orphaned files build up unseen' is wrong: the stage directory is deterministic per descriptor (service.py:3400 'download-{fingerprint}'), so a retry reuses and truncates it rather than adding a new one. (2) 'Already staged: 0.0 MiB' is accurate, not a miscount. Resume checkpoints are per file: the fetch-state sidecar records bytes_done only after a file finishes (acquisition.py:1311-1333). In homes/res6 the sidecar lists only config.json and vocab.txt (about 9 KB), so the 120 MB partial encoder file earns no credit and the file restarts from zero. The real defect is that the checkpoints are too coarse (no mid-file checkpoints) for a 630 MiB single file. The staging GC runs only from Lab ▸ Models reconcile (model_installed_view.py:1809), as stated.
evidence: reports/live-power-user.md §4 'Interrupted rerun' (169 MB left in staging)
homes/res6/.../staging/download-09a5f117.../state/fetch-state.json (only config.json and vocab.txt recorded; the encoder has no entry)
tracked_task: none (TASK-33079 AC#2, To Do, covers partial-file cleanup only when one of two concurrent installs fails)
root_cause: Staging GC runs only when the Lab > Models installed view calls ModelArtifactService.reconcile(). The wizard never reconciles or resumes, and preflight does not count the orphan as staged bytes.
solution: When the Speech step shows, run reconcile() for this artifact in a worker (or a scoped resume probe). If a resumable partial exists, show 'A previous download stopped at 129 of 633 MiB. [Resume download] [Discard partial]', make preflight's 'Already staged' include it, and resume with HTTP Range if the acquisition supports it; otherwise discard it. Clean staging on Cancel (voice-speech-09) and on an orderly app shutdown during a download. The fix lives in the shared artifact layer, so Lab > Models installs benefit too.
solution_review: Better root-cause fix in the shared acquisition layer: periodically fsync and checkpoint bytes_done (and the validators) mid-file, every N MiB, so the existing Range-resume path actually resumes the large file. Showing 'A previous download stopped at X of 633 MiB [Resume]' then comes almost for free, because preflight already credits checkpointed bytes. Running reconcile() from the wizard is not needed for correctness, since a retry reuses the stage.

cluster: Config encryption lifecycle is half-built
title: Startup unlock has no recovery: a wrong or forgotten password leaves no way into the app
problem: The packaged path asks once, before the TUI, with getpass: 'Configuration password: ' (launcher.py:55). A wrong password, an empty entry, Ctrl+C or a missing private terminal all return 'configuration_unlock_failed'. cli.py then runs minimal_recovery, whose RecoveryApp composes 'Recovery required: configuration_unlock_failed' and immediately pushes BackupRestoreScreen over it (launcher.py:120-130). Nothing says the password was wrong, nothing offers another try, and nothing lets the user start without the encrypted keys. The setup dialog promises 'If you forget it, the encrypted keys cannot be recovered — you'll need to re-enter them.' In practice a forgotten password blocks the whole app, not just the keys, and the app offers no way to re-enter them. Naming also drifts: setup calls it a 'master password', the module path's prompt is titled 'Unlock Configuration', and the packaged prompt asks for a 'Configuration password'.
impact: First-time: one typo at launch lands them in Backup & Restore with no hint that the password was the problem, and a forgotten password looks like data loss. Power user: there is no scripted or non-TTY unlock; getpass refuses without a private terminal and that also routes to recovery mode. Violates Nielsen #9 (recover from errors), #1 (status), #2 (raw error code instead of plain language) and #4 (three names for one password).
correction: 'One typo ... leaves no way into the app' is overstated. problem: Success only updates the status line. The button keeps its 'Set a password' label and focus while the hint reads 'Enter / Ctrl+N next · Ctrl+B back · Esc exit setup', so Enter, meant as 'continue', reopens 'Set up master password' (live). Submitting again calls enable_config_encryption a second time. encrypt_api_keys_in_config regenerates password_verifier for the new password (config.py:1101-1104) but leaves values that are already enc: untouched (1124-1132), so with a different password the keys become unreadable while the new password 'works'. On a re-run, on_show decides through stored_plaintext_key_present, which returns False whenever encryption is enabled (first_run_setup_state.py:1392-1393). The step therefore says 'No API keys saved yet — nothing to protect.' about keys that are saved and encrypted, or offers 'Set a password' as if none existed.
impact: First-time: reads the reopened dialog as 'did it fail?'. Typing a password again, especially a different one, silently breaks the keys they just protected, and the next launch accepts the new password but the providers fail. Power user re-running setup: is told nothing is saved. Violates Nielsen #1 (status), #5 (error prevention) and #4 (the hint line contradicts what Enter does on this focus).
correction: The consequence is worse than the issue claims, and some details differ. The second enable_config_encryption writes the new verifier to disk and only then fails to publish the runtime config ('Configuration runtime reload failed'), so it returns False. The step then shows both '✓ Encryption enabled.' and 'Enabling encryption failed — your keys are unchanged (plain text).' The second message is false: the key on disk is enc:, encrypted under the first password. After that, Next shows 'Saving setup progress failed. Retry before continuing.' and Exit setup shows the toast 'Setup progress could not be saved. Retry Exit setup.'. The new password does NOT 'work' at the next launch: the packaged preflight's strict decrypt fails, so both passwords send the user to recovery mode. The live part as claimed holds: after success, focus stays on 'Set a password' and Enter reopens 'Set up master password'. The re-run 'No API keys saved yet' state for an encrypted config is a code-only claim and matches first_run_setup_state.py:1392-1393. Mechanism (re-verified separately as new-protect-summary-01): Every claim reproduced independently (fresh profile vn1-b, 120x40, OpenAI with a fake key, Continue anyway, Protect, password A, then Enter, which reopens the dialog, then password B). The step showed both '✓ Encryption enabled.' and 'Enabling encryption failed — your keys are unchanged (plain text).' On disk the verifier had changed while the key stayed 'enc:' under A: A fails the verifier but decrypts the key, and B passes the verifier but cannot decrypt it. Corrections and additions: (1) Only a different second password triggers this. A pure probe shows that re-entering the same password returns True and later writes succeed. (2) The trap is wider than Next and Exit setup. Voice Next fails with 'Saving the Voice settings failed. Retry.  Retry with Next, or go Back.', and Skip setup on Welcome fails with 'Setup completion could not be saved. Retry before closing.' Back still navigates. Ctrl+Q exits with EXITED:0. (3) Later writes fail before touching disk: config.toml's hash was unchanged across Next, Voice, Exit setup and Skip setup. The cause is that every mutation strict-decrypts the raw file with the in-process password (config.py:7630-7639, 'Authoritative configuration could not be decrypted'). So the session is poisoned, but no further damage is done. (4) Why the poisoning persists: enable_config_encryption calls set_encryption_password(B) before _publish_runtime_config_unlocked, and on failure it neither reverts the in-process password nor restores the file (config.py:9729-9742). (5) This duplicates protect-summary-04, whose correction already documents the write-before-publish failure, the false 'unchanged (plain text)' line, both retry messages and the dual-password preflight failure. Merge it there and carry over the only new design point: a persistent write failure leaves no way out of the wizard without saving.

The plain-text location (~/.config/tldw_cli/config.toml) and who can read it are never stated. The Provider step said only 'Key staged — it will be checked when you continue.' (static-code-map-49, provider area). The cost of choosing a password is stated only as 'You'll be asked for this password each time chatbook starts.', and the dialog's forgot-password line understates the consequence (see 02).
impact: First-time (Sam, 'feel sure the key is safe'): can't weigh plain text against a password, so may encrypt without understanding the startup cost, or skip without understanding the exposure. Violates Nielsen #2 (match the real world), #6 (recognition over recall: the hidden skip) and #10.
correction: 'Nothing says ... that it is plain text in config.toml' is wrong. Protect says 'Encrypt the API keys in your config file … Skip to leave keys as plain text'. The Summary shows '✗ Key encryption — API keys are stored as plain text' when a plaintext key is stored (cloud2/19) and a 'Config file: <path>' footer. These parts hold: no file path on Protect; Provider says only 'Key staged — it will be checked when you continue.'; and 'Skip' names a control that does not exist (the footer is ← Back / Next → / Exit setup).
evidence: reports/live-resilience.md §5 (plaintext api_key with credential_source stored, file 0600)
tracked_task: none
root_cause: The copy was written for the spec's Back / Next / Skip footer (spec D4), which shipped as Back / Next / Exit setup.
solution: Rewrite the stored-key state. Title: 'Protect your API key'. Body: 'Your OpenAI key is saved as plain text in <full config path, wrapped>. Any program or person using your account can read it. Encrypt it with a master password and chatbook will ask for that password each time it starts.' Use two explicit buttons: primary 'Encrypt with a password…' and secondary 'Keep as plain text'. The secondary advances like Next and records the choice, so Summary can say '– Key encryption — off (your choice)'. Name every provider whose key is stored. Pair with 02's honest forgot-password line in the dialog.
solution_review: Two explicit buttons ('Encrypt with a password…' / 'Keep as plain text') are right and also fix the phantom Skip. Keep the body short, at two sentences; the full path can go on a second dim line. Recording the explicit choice for the Summary is a nice touch, but it is optional.

cluster: Setup session has no lifecycle model: re-run, resume and exits ignore existing state
title: Esc or 'Review settings' on Summary leaves setup unfinished; next launch nags to resume
problem: Esc still runs action_cancel on the Summary. There is no Summary branch, so it opens 'Exit setup?' and confirming dismisses with None; first_run.setup_completed is never written. The next launch shows 'Continue setup?… A previous setup stopped before it finished.' 'Review settings' does the same by design (completed: False, category providers-models), and its label promises general settings but opens Providers & Models only. The source comment on SUMMARY_KEY_HINTS says Esc 'goes inert' on the Summary, but the only test checks the hint string, not the behaviour. The user guide says 'Escape asks before leaving setup' and lists 'Review settings' as an ordinary exit.
impact: First-time: after finishing, is told setup is incomplete and asked again at every launch, and may redo setup. Power user: Esc, the natural 'done' key, silently undoes completion. Violates Nielsen #4 (consistency: Esc means different things on different steps), #1 and #5.
correction: Live with a COMPLETE provider and model (llama.cpp on my fake server). This rules out the possibility that the resilience capture's nag came from an incomplete provider. On the Summary, Esc gives 'Exit setup? Your provider and model are saved. Other completed setup steps are also saved, and you can continue from Settings ▸ Diagnostics.' After confirming: config has setup_started only, and refresh_consent_recorded=false. The relaunch shows 'Continue setup? A previous setup stopped before it finished…'. After 'Later' and another relaunch it appears again. 'Resume' lands on the Summary, which the issue did not mention. The 'Review settings' path (completed: False) is code-only and correct (FirstRunSetupWizard.py:9977-9987).
tracked_task: none (task-25821, Done, declined a Finish button on the assumption that Esc was inert)
root_cause: FirstRunSetupWizard.action_cancel has no STEP_SUMMARY branch. open_provider_settings deliberately dismisses with completed=False. Both were written before the Summary counted as a completed setup.
solution: Send every Summary exit through one finish path that writes setup_completed and the model-list consent. Esc on the Summary opens 'Finish setup? Your choices are saved. You'll land on Home.' with [Finish] and [Keep reviewing]; Finish calls _finalize(TAB_HOME). Rename 'Review settings' to 'Open Settings'; it should _finalize and then open Settings ▸ Overview, or Providers & Models only when the provider row needs attention. Change SUMMARY_KEY_HINTS to 'Ctrl+B back · Esc finish · or choose an action below' and fix the stale comment. Replace the string-only test with one that presses Esc on the Summary, confirms, and asserts setup_completed=true and no recovery dialog on the next mount. Document both behaviours in First_Run_Setup.md. The same path fixes 11's dropped interview and 17's unrecorded consent.
solution_review: One finish path that writes setup_completed and consent is right. For Esc, the most proportionate fix is to do what TASK-25821's comment and the current hint already promise: make Esc inert on the Summary (one guard in action_cancel), or finalize to Home with a toast and no extra dialog. A 'Finish setup?' confirm adds a modal to a step whose hint already says 'choose an action below to finish'. 'Review settings' should finalize before opening Settings. Renaming it 'Open Settings' is fine.

problem: Every power-user run in this review was a re-run, and each Summary shows the first-run exit set with no 'Done'. title: Unfinished setup nags every launch: 'Later' saves nothing, other states loop or go silent
problem: The recovery logic has no 'deferred' state. 'Later' (and Esc, which is bound to Later) returns without writing anything, so setup_recovery_action returns 'prompt' again on the next launch. setup_started is written as soon as the wizard mounts, so a user who quits on Welcome has no draft and gets the 'Setup isn't finished' toast forever. A resume that crashed leaves resume_attempted=True, which maps to the 'home' action, and that action has no UI at all. All three states force Home (app.py:2776-2782) and block the startup catalog refresh (setup_owns_startup_networking).
impact: First-time: repeated interruptions teach reflexive dismissal; after a crash there is no pointer at all, and every launch quietly returns to Home. Power user: default_tab is ignored and model lists never refresh, with no visible cause. Violates User control and freedom (#3), Visibility of system status (#1), and Aesthetic and minimalist design (#8, needless interruptions).
correction: State A is confirmed live. State B is confirmed live, but the claim that 'in A, B and C the route is forced to Home and catalog networking is suppressed' is wrong for B. B maps to action 'none', so default_tab is respected (relaunch landed on Console) and networking is not suppressed (app.py:2776-2782 and app_feature_glue.py:60-72 only cover offer/prompt/home). State C is code-only, and its window is narrow: resume_attempted is cleared as soon as the resumed step mounts (FirstRunSetupWizard.py:10073-10113), so C needs a crash between Resume and that mount. Also notable for B: Ctrl+Q on Welcome quits instantly, and the auto-offer is permanently consumed because setup_started is written on mount.

'later' is not persisted. should_show_resume_toast has no cap. _maybe_offer_first_run_wizard has no branch for 'home'. setup_started is persisted in on_mount before any user input. _resolve_initial_shell_route and setup_owns_startup_networking treat prompt and home as 'setup owns this launch' indefinitely.
solution: Add one persisted snooze, [first_run] resume_deferred = true plus resume_reminders_shown = N. 1) 'Later' (and Esc) writes resume_deferred. Later launches show no modal. Instead, one non-modal line appears in the Console 'Get started' card or a Home banner: 'Setup paused at Provider (step 2 of 6) · [Continue setup] [Dismiss]'. Dismiss deletes the draft, leaving the Settings route. 2) Rename the dialog's Later button to 'Not now'. 3) Write setup_started only after the first successful Next on Welcome, so quitting on Welcome re-offers the wizard once instead of nagging. 4) Cap the 'Setup isn't finished' toast at two launches, using a stored counter. 5) Give the 'home' action the same banner ('Setup was interrupted · [Continue setup] [Start over]'). 6) Stop forcing TAB_HOME and stop suppressing catalog networking once the user has deferred; respect default_tab.

Writing setup_started only after the first Next on Welcome is the highest-value, lowest-risk change: it fixes B and keeps the auto-offer for someone who just quit. A persisted snooze for 'Later' plus a non-modal 'Continue setup (Provider)' row in Console's existing Get started card is proportionate, and reuses the ADR-210 catch instead of adding a Home banner. 'Not now' is a better label. Capping the toast at two launches is fine but redundant once B is fixed. Point 6 (stop forcing TAB_HOME after a deferral) is right. Do not delete the draft on 'Dismiss' without a confirm: it is the only memory of the user's choices.

correction: Small precision issue: the dialog says 'Resume from the last completed step', but the draft stores the step the user was on (active_step_id). Exiting at Provider stored active_step_id='provider', where nothing was completed. So the copy is wrong in both directions, not only 'one step before'. The 'staged only in this wizard … non-secret setup progress' exit copy appears only when a key was typed. Without a key, the exit copy is 'Steps you've already completed are saved. cluster: No end-to-end 'first chat works' contract across Summary and handoff
title: Setup finishes with ✓ and 'Start chatting', but the first chat is blocked (no context window, non-chat models, no end-to-end readiness check)
problem: The wizard declares success while the first message cannot be sent. Summary: '✓ Provider — openai', '✓ Default model — tts-1-hd-1106', with 'Start chatting' as the primary action. The first send returns 'System: This request cannot fit the selected model. Response reservation and safety margin leave no model input capacity. Summarizing older turns cannot make enough room. Repair the model limit, reduce mandatory context or the response maximum, or allow older turns to be omitted.' The composer then shows 'Send blocked — resolve response recovery first'. The prefilled default gpt-5.6-terra fails identically; the switcher shows it and its siblings (gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-luna) as '~4k'. A clean Full run with gpt-5.4-mini was also blocked. Only gpt-4.1-mini, picked by hand in Console, replied ('Hello there! Hope you're well.'), 621 s after launch.
impact: First-time (Sam) follows every recommendation and gets a ✓ Summary. Then comes a jargon error and a stuck composer. Recovery needed Retry, Discard, Ctrl+T, Alt+M, a search and 6 arrow presses, and most users would conclude the key or the app is broken. Power user (Riley): a Summary ✓ is no evidence of anything, so they must debug context budgets in the first minute. Violates H1 Visibility of system status (✓ means 'saved', not 'works'), H5 Error prevention (a non-chat or unsized model is accepted) and H9 Help users recognize, diagnose and recover from errors.
correction: Root cause is upstream of the wizard and more specific than stated. Utils/token_counter.py:497-503 has PROVIDER_CONTEXT_WINDOWS['openai'] = 4096, the 'API default' tier of resolve_context_window (:527-564). Every OpenAI id missing from MODEL_TOKEN_LIMITS and DEFAULT_MODEL_CAPABILITIES (all gpt-5*, chatgpt-4o-latest, tts-*) resolves to exactly 4096. [api_settings.openai] max_tokens = 4096 (config.py:4546), so console_context_policy.py:293-302 computes window − reservation − margin ≤ 0. This is NOT a TASK-32709 regression. Its AC#2 is 'model/API defaults then exactly 32000', and its own follow-up commit 325f2473ab moved the openai 4096 row into token_counter. The 32000 fallback applies only to providers without a row. Scope is provider-specific: the same wizard path with Anthropic's '(recommended)' claude-sonnet-5-5 replied 'OK' (anthropic fallback 200000). gpt-5.6-terra is a real, listed model (in OpenAI's live /v1/models, 137 ids), so the block is purely the pre-send capacity check. The Summary is not purely config-presence: it already swaps 'Start chatting' for 'Review provider setup' when Provider is ✗. It just has no capacity or chat-capability check.

root_cause: Each step validates a local fact: the key was accepted, the model id is in the list. The Summary then ticks rows from config presence (first_run_setup_state.py:1838-2031). No step asks Console's send preflight whether a turn can actually be sent. Two upstream defects then make failure certain. First, Model tags discovery row 0 as '(recommended)' with no chat-capability filter (FirstRunSetupWizard.py:3812-3814). Second, the curated OpenAI defaults have no context_window (model_capabilities.py:94), so the budget falls back to about 4k. Against api_settings.openai.max_tokens = 4096 that leaves zero input capacity.
solution: Add a final 'Ready to chat?' check to the Summary. Compute it with the same preflight Console runs before a send (context-budget resolution plus model capability classification), not a wizard copy. UI: a top Summary row reading either '✓ Ready to chat — OpenAI · gpt-4.1-mini (1M context)' or '✗ Can't chat yet — gpt-5.6-terra's context size is unknown, so every message would be blocked.', with [Choose another model] (returns to Model with the reason pinned) and [Set context size…]. Optionally, behind the consent copy 'Send a one-word test message? Uses a few tokens.', run a 1-token completion and show the reply latency. 'Start chatting' stays primary only when the check passes; otherwise the primary becomes 'Fix model'. Run the same capability check when the Model step commits, with inline copy such as 'tts-1-hd-1106 is a speech model, not a chat model — pick another.' This one fix covers the non-chat '(recommended)' acceptance, the unusable default model and the Summary over-claim (model and summary areas). Upstream, also add context_window for every curated default and a CI check that each resolves to more than max_tokens.
solution_review: Split the fix. The P0 fix is small and belongs in the catalog, not in an L-sized wizard gate. (1) Drop or raise the stale openai 4096 'API default' so unknown OpenAI models fall to the 32000 estimated fallback, or 128k. (2) Add ^gpt-5/^gpt-6/^chatgpt patterns and a context_window for gpt-5.6-terra (model_capabilities.py:94). (3) When the window is only estimated, cap the response reservation, e.g. min(max_tokens, window/4), so no unknown model is ever pre-blocked to zero. (4) Add the proposed test that every shipped default resolves a window larger than its provider's max_tokens (no test pins the 4096 today). That alone fixes the env-key path the wizard never sees. The wizard 'Ready to chat?' Summary row is right as defence-in-depth, and is M rather than L if it calls resolve_context_window/resolve_request_capacity offline. Filter non-chat ids (tts, whisper, transcribe, embedding, dall-e, realtime, moderation) out of the '(recommended)' slot, which is just API row 0 (FirstRunSetupWizard.py:3812-3814), and prefer the curated default there. Keep the 1-token test optional and behind consent.

cluster: Commit-on-Next overloads 'Next' and keeps no draft ledger
title: Next silently means skip, save defaults, or refuse depending on the step; no explicit Skip
problem: Welcome promises '…most steps can be skipped with Next'. On Provider, Next with no key shows 'API key required. Set OPENAI_API_KEY or add api_key under [api_settings.openai].  Retry with Next, or go Back.' indefinitely. Only Enter inside the empty key field skips, and a mouse user has no skip at all. On Model, Next with no model chosen skips the step and silently discards the staged provider and key: the Summary reads '✗ Provider — no credentials or saved endpoint' and chat_defaults stays the template OpenAI / gpt-5.6-terra, even for a working local Ollama/llama.cpp. Voice says 'skip with Next if you don't want voice', but Next writes [app_tts] OPENAI_BASE_URL = http://127.0.0.1:8765/v1/audio/speech, and the Summary then claims '✓ Voice — PocketTTS (default voice)'. Protect says 'Skip to leave keys as plain text', but there is no Skip control.
impact: First-time users cannot predict whether Next will save, skip or block. A mouse-only user is stuck on Provider, and a local user's working connection is lost on Next. Power users find that an untouched Voice step on a re-run breaks a working OpenAI TTS endpoint, and cancelling does not undo it. Violates H5 Error prevention, H3 User control and freedom (no explicit skip, no undo), H4 Consistency and standards and H1 Visibility of system status.
correction: (1) Provider is not a dead end. The key field's own hint says 'No key yet? Enter skips this step — you can add a provider later in Settings.', and Exit setup works. The gap is the missing clickable skip; every terminal user has an Enter key. (2) 'Retry with Next' can succeed once a key is pasted. (3) The Model skip discards the staged provider, but the Summary shows it ('✗ Provider' plus 'Review provider setup'), and the key is still staged if the user goes Back. (4) The Voice write is worse than described because it is a hybrid. The base URL is PocketTTS while default_model = 'tts-1-hd', default_voice = 'shimmer' and default_format = 'mp3' are OpenAI values, and the draft says pocket-tts / alba / wav.

config after Model skip: [chat_defaults] still provider 'OpenAI' / model 'gpt-5.6-terra'; no anthropic api_key written
tracked_task: none for the cross-step semantics. Symptoms: TASK-26837 (To Do; tested provider written nowhere), TASK-25820 (Done, closed INVALID; pinned Model skip-safe as intended), TASK-32555 (Done; added the Enter-in-empty-field skip).
root_cause: The footer has no Skip action, only Back / Next / Exit (FirstRunSetupWizard.py:8010-8014). As a result each step overloads commit() to mean 'skip' in its own way. ProviderStep.commit refuses when the provider isn't ready (:3248-3263). ModelStep.commit returns (True, "") with no model and drops the staged provider+model pair (:4194-4198). VoiceSetupStep.commit always posts STTSSettingsSaveEvent for PocketTTS, OpenAI and Custom (:5127-5167). On top of that, _advance appends 'Retry with Next, or go Back.' to every refusal (:9874).
solution:
Separate the two intents in the footer. Add a 'Skip step' button between Back and Next, on every step except Welcome and Summary, bound to Alt+S and listed in the hint line. Its contract: nothing from this step is saved, and the outcome is recorded as 'skipped'. Next then means 'save what you chose and continue'; label it 'Save & continue' when the step will write and 'Continue' when it won't (from a step.will_write() query). Per step:
- Provider: Skip clears the selection (today's skip_without_key) and is reachable by mouse. Next with no key shows the inline 'Paste a key above, or choose Skip step.'
- Model: when a provider is staged, Skip asks 'Skip choosing a model? Your OpenAI key won't be saved. [Use the recommended model] [Skip and discard key]'. Saving the provider without a model is preferable if the persistence layer allows it.
- Voice: Next on an untouched step writes nothing (a delta commit, as Tools already does); Skip writes nothing.
- Protect: copy changes to 'Choose Skip step to keep keys as plain text'.
- Welcome: copy changes to 'Every step can be skipped — Next saves what you chose.'
This one fix removes the Provider dead end, the silent key drop and the Voice clobber (provider, model and voice areas).
solution_review: Right direction, but a third footer button on every step adds chrome for one real problem. More proportionate: (a) delta-commit Voice so an untouched step writes nothing, as Tools and Appearance already do; (b) on Model with a staged provider, pre-select the recommended chat row so Next saves it, and if the user clears it, refuse inline with 'Pick a model to save your Anthropic key — or skip'; (c) add a visible 'Skip this step' link only where Next refuses, in the Provider key panel; (d) fix the Welcome and Protect copy ('Next without a password keeps keys as plain text'). cluster: Highlight drives selection and focused widgets swallow Enter
title: Enter is advertised as 'next' but selects, tests, skips the provider or saves instead, depending on the focused widget
problem:
Every step shows 'Enter / Ctrl+N next · Ctrl+B back · Esc exit setup', but Enter does five different things:
(a) On the Provider list it selects the highlighted row and never advances. With a detected server, it selected the pre-highlighted OpenAI and the banner 'Found a local endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:9099.' disappeared.
(b) In the key field, with a key typed, it runs a probe ('Testing…' then '✓ Reached the server, but your chosen model was not in its list. Pick one on the next step.'). A second Enter re-tests; it never advances.
(c) In the empty key field it skips the whole provider.
(d) On a freshly rendered Model list it advances without selecting the '(recommended)' row, so nothing is saved.
(e) In Voice 'Sample text' or the endpoint field it saves the voice and advances.
The guide repeats 'Enter continues to the next step (from a choice list or a text field…)'.
impact: First-time: Sam pressed Enter in the key field twice, saw nothing happen, and had to discover the mouse. Jo lost a detected server with one key press and later lost the provider on the Model step. Power users can't build muscle memory, and an accidental Enter in a text field commits the Voice step. Violates H4 Consistency and standards, H1 Visibility of system status (the hint is wrong) and H5 Error prevention.
correction: (e) is not a defect. Enter in Voice 'Sample text' saving and advancing is exactly what the hint ('Enter … next') and the guide ('from a … text field') promise. It is the deliberate TASK-21142 / UAT N-1 'form + Enter = continue' contract (FirstRunSetupWizard.py:8018-8052). (c) is announced in the key field's own hint. (d) loses nothing for OpenAI: the custom field is prefilled with gpt-5.6-terra and Enter commits it (which then hits the P0). The loss is for providers with no prefill (Anthropic, local servers). The 'Found a local endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:9099.' banner in this verification came from a sibling verifier's server, but its disappearing when Enter selects OpenAI is product behaviour.
evidence: tldw_chatbook/UI/Wizards/FirstRunSetupWizard.py:224-247 (SetupRadioSet selects only if a highlight exists), :3791-3792 (_render_models resets _selected = None)
evidence/verify-cross-cutting/30-run2-provider.txt → 31-run2-provider-enter-on-list.txt (Enter selects OpenAI, banner gone, stays on Provider)
tracked_task: none. TASK-21142 (Done) and TASK-32555 (Done) created today's per-widget Enter behaviour.
root_cause: SetupWizardContainer binds Enter to next (FirstRunSetupWizard.py:8024), but the focused widget consumes Enter first. Textual's OptionList binds Enter to select (_option_list.py:115). The key field has its own probe handler (:3061-3065), and _advance_on_input_submit special-cases it, skipping the provider when the field is empty (:8033-8052). SetupRadioSet.action_request_advance selects only when a highlight exists (:224-247), but _render_models resets RadioSet._selected to None (:3791-3792), so Enter advances with nothing selected. Every other Input submit calls action_next. The hint line is a static string per step (:8840-8852).
solution:
Define one Enter contract and make the hint describe the focused control.
- Provider list: Enter selects the row, then advances if the provider is ready. Otherwise it moves focus to the key field, or to 'Use this server' when a server was detected.
- Key field: Enter means 'check key, then continue'. Run the probe, advance automatically on ✓, and stay with an inline error on ✗ ('✗ OpenAI rejected this key — paste it again').
- Empty key field: Enter focuses the Skip step button (cross-cutting-03) and shows 'Press Enter again to skip OpenAI', instead of skipping silently.
- Model list: after rendering, put the highlight on the current or recommended row so that Enter selects it. Enter never advances with nothing selected while a provider is staged.
- Other free-text inputs (sample text, endpoint, model id): Enter moves focus to the next control instead of committing the step.
- Hint line: make it context-aware: 'Enter check key · Ctrl+N next' in the key field, 'Enter choose · Ctrl+N next' on lists, 'Enter next' on radio groups.
Update the 'Keyboard' section of First_Run_Setup.md. Pairs with cross-cutting-06 (arrow keys).
solution_review: Keep the Model fix: after render, seat the highlight and selection on the current or recommended chat row. Keep 'check, then continue on ✓' for the key field. Keep the context-aware hint. Drop the proposal that Enter in free-text inputs should only move focus: it reverses an accepted UAT decision, breaks the form-submit convention and adds keystrokes. Don't make empty-key Enter a two-press confirmation either; the hint promises a one-press skip and TASK-32555 just shipped it.

title: Browsing a list selects every highlighted row, fires network discovery, leaves errors behind and wipes typed values
problem: After the first interaction, every arrow press selects a provider, re-lays out the panel and starts model discovery. Passing Baidu Qianfan shows 'Couldn't discover models for Baidu Qianfan. Set QIANFAN_API_KEY or add api_key under [api_settings.qianfan]. Or go Back.' Passing Arcee leaves the same message for ARCEE_API_KEY. Reaching OpenRouter takes 32 presses, each one a discovery request; with an env key exported, that is a call to the provider. Before the first interaction, OpenAI looks highlighted but is not selected, so Next skips the provider. On Model, one Down press clears the prefilled custom model with no warning. The provider list (OptionList) and the model list (RadioSet) on adjacent steps use different selection models.
impact: First-time users read errors about providers they never chose, and the 'Found a local endpoint' banner disappears while they browse. Power users trigger 32 network calls and flickering errors to reach one row, and lose the prefilled value. This contradicts the guide's 'no probe traffic leaves your machine without your action'. Violates H1 Visibility of system status (highlight and selection look alike), H4 Consistency, H5 Error prevention and H8 Aesthetic and minimalist design.
correction: A network request per row only happens for rows whose credentials are already present (env keys) or for loopback endpoints. Keyless cloud rows fail the local readiness check without a request. So '32 network calls' holds only with many provider keys exported, and loopback probes don't leave the machine. The cited Arcee capture (live-power-user/11) shows the error for the currently selected row (Arcee's endpoint is displayed), not a stale one.
tracked_task: none. TASK-21142 (Done; UAT N-8) introduced selection-follows-highlight for radio groups.
root_cause: ProviderStep._on_provider_highlighted selects on highlight once _provider_choice_interacted is set (FirstRunSetupWizard.py:2934-2950), and select_provider starts an 8 s discovery worker (:2369-2577). SetupRadioSet selects on every arrow press (WAI-ARIA radio pattern, :214-243), and the wizard applies it the same way to 2-option groups and to 20-row model lists. A model radio and the custom Input are mutually exclusive, so selecting a radio clears the input.
solution:
Use the right pattern for each list size. Short radio groups (6 options or fewer: track, voice service, language, precision) keep selection-follows-highlight. Long lists (Provider, Model, RAG, and the 'Show all' theme and card lists) become listboxes:
- Arrows only move the highlight; Enter, Space or a click selects.
- The selected row carries a '●' marker that looks different from the highlight bar.
- The highlighted row gets neutral preview copy ('OpenAI — needs an API key', 'Ollama — local, no key').
- Discovery starts only on selection, debounced by 400 ms.
On Model, a list pick replaces the custom field only on Enter or click, and arrowing never clears a typed value. Preselect a detected or current provider so the initial state is a real selection. Update the guide's 'Arrow keys select' line.
solution_review: Making the Provider OptionList highlight-only (Enter or click selects), with debounced discovery, is the right minimal fix. It is OptionList's native behaviour before the custom select-on-highlight (:2934-2950). Converting Model, RAG and theme lists wholesale to listboxes reverses TASK-21142 and isn't needed if (a) the custom model input is cleared only by an explicit pick, never by arrowing, and (b) lists render with the current or recommended row already selected.

problem:

Draft checkpoints copy free text (voice sample_text: 'Hello from Chatbook.') into config.toml. The Exit dialog shown during a 633 MiB Speech download says nothing about the download.
impact: Power users must diff config.toml to learn what setup did, and there is no undo for an exploratory run. For first-time users 'saved' is abstract, so they can't tell what to fix. Violates H1 Visibility of system status, H3 User control and freedom (no undo) and H10 Help and documentation (no record of changes).
correction: 'No screen lists what was written' overstates it. The Summary does read back provider, model, voice, RAG, theme and encryption from persisted config. What is missing is any mention of side-effect writes ([tts_settings] duplication, the transcribe.cpp path, draft free text) and a list of what was saved in the Exit dialog.
tracked_task: none
root_cause: The commit-on-Next model (FirstRunSetupWizard.py:9862-9902) keeps no session-level ledger. commit_config (:10155-10242) is the only audited writer; STTS (stts_events.py:1953-2080), transcribe_cpp_config.py:29-46, enable_config_encryption and _persist_started_flag (:10714-10739) all bypass it. The draft allowlist includes voice sample_text (first_run_setup_state.py:995-1005).
solution:
Add a setup-session change ledger. Snapshot the config when the wizard mounts; every writer (commit_config and the four out-of-band paths) appends {section.key: old → new}. In the UI:
1. After a step commits, show a dim one-line note in the step footer, e.g. 'Saved: voice → PocketTTS at 127.0.0.1:8765'.
2. The Exit dialog lists the ledger, e.g. 'Saved this session: provider + model (OpenAI · gpt-5.4-mini) · voice (PocketTTS) · theme (nord). The Parakeet v2 download is still running.' Offer an optional 'Undo this session's changes', which restores the snapshot and names what can't be undone (encryption, downloaded models).
3. The Summary gets a 'View changes (12 settings)' expander showing the diff.
Also drop sample_text from drafts, and route the out-of-band writers through commit_config, or at least through the ledger.
solution_review: A full ledger with 'Undo this session' is L and risky: restoring a snapshot races other writers (Settings, Console) and can't undo encryption or downloads. A proportionate order: (1) Voice delta-commit, which removes the biggest silent write; (2) drop sample_text from the draft allowlist (first_run_setup_state.py:995-1005); (3) have the Exit dialog list the saved areas from wizard_data; (4) only then consider a ledger.
