root_cause:
The frame's height is fixed and never adapts to the terminal height:
- '.wizard-title' is 3 rows (_wizards.tcss:1393-1397).
- The tracker can take up to 5 rows (:1315-1320).
- '.wizard-navigation' is 4 rows, but its buttons are only 1 row tall (:1405-1410).
- The container has a border and 'padding: 2' (BaseWizard.py:62-69).
- The docked hint row adds 1 (:1304-1311).

Summary's two action rows are docked to the bottom with 'margin-bottom: 1' on each row and 'padding-bottom: 1' (:1165-1178). Radio and checkbox labels are single-line ToggleButton labels, so they truncate instead of wrapping. When focus moves into view it scrolls the content above it off screen.

Add a 'short' layout tier, switched on in on_resize when the screen is under 30 rows. Do this the way _sync_compact_mode already works: add a '-short' class to SetupWizardContainer.
1. Merge the title and tracker into one row: 'Set up tldw chatbook · Step 2 of 6 · Provider   ✓ ● ○ ○ ○ ○'.
2. Make the nav bar 1 row (height 1, no blank padding rows). In short mode drop the outer border and padding ('border: none; padding: 0 1').
3. Merge the key-hint row and the size-hint row into one (a11y-03).

That gives back about 9 rows, so the step gets about 19 of 24 rows, roughly twice what it has now.

On Summary in short mode:
- Use one docked action row: the primary button plus a 'More ▾' button that opens an OptionList popover (Add your first document / Write your first note / Explore Home / Review settings).
- Remove the row margins and the bottom padding.
- Make the read-back the scroll area, and scroll it to the first ✗/! row on mount.

- Move the keyword to the front of the radio label: 'Quick setup (recommended) — provider, model, voice, protection'.
- Shorten the consent label to 'Keep model lists fresh (checks online at startup)'.
- On Provider, put the probe result after the key field, or re-anchor scroll so the error line stays above the focused field.

This one tier also fixes a11y-02 and a11y-03. Add a pilot test at 80x24 that asserts at least 8 Summary read-back rows are visible and the first ✗ row is on screen.
solution_review: The direction is right: a '-short' class set on resize, following the _sync_compact_mode precedent. Four concerns. (a) A one-row merged title+tracker must keep the amber '!' attention state from TASK-21143 and the current step's name. The proposed '✓ ● ○' glyph row drops '!'. (b) Hiding 'Add your first document / Write your first note' behind 'More ▾' undoes the deliberate visible exits from task-32072 and task-32140. Instead, remove the row margins and padding-bottom (about 3 rows) and drop the outer border in short mode (2 rows). That reaches about 8 read-back rows without a popover. (c) A 1-row nav in short mode conflicts with a11y-10's 3-row bordered nav buttons, so pick one 1-row secondary treatment. (d) 'Scroll to first ✗' needs line arithmetic, because all rows are one Static (#setup-summary-rows). Listing ✗/! rows first is simpler. Also add a pilot assertion that the key input is visible on Provider while a pinned error is showing.

correction: The cause is more specific. Textual's Screen.set_focus calls scroll_to_center(widget, origin_visible=True) whenever the focused widget is not fully visible (textual/screen.py:1138-1145). Centring is why it overshoots: at 100x30 there are 3 blank rows under 'Restore a backup' while the heading is hidden. Reproduced on 4 fresh launches: 80x24 starts at 'Next — Esc exits setup.' (2 of 2) and 100x30 starts at 'all in your terminal.' (2 of 2).
evidence: tldw_chatbook/UI/Wizards/FirstRunSetupWizard.py:9312-9342 (show_step focuses the preferred target with target.focus())
tldw_chatbook/UI/Wizards/FirstRunSetupWizard.py:7368-7404 (Welcome: heading, two subtitles, then the radio set and Restore a backup at the bottom)
tracked_task: none
root_cause: show_step() calls `target.focus()` with Textual's default `scroll_visible=True` (FirstRunSetupWizard.py:9342). The preferred focus target on Welcome is the track radio set, which sits at the bottom of the step. When the step is taller than the viewport, scrolling it into view pushes the heading off the top. Nothing scrolls the step back to its top after that.
solution: In show_step(), call `target.focus(scroll_visible=False)`, then `current_step.scroll_home(animate=False)`. Only if the target is still entirely outside the visible region, call `scroll_to_widget(target, top=False)` for the smallest scroll that shows it. Always scroll Welcome home. With the short tier from a11y-01, all of Welcome fits at 80x24. Add a pilot test at 100x30 and 80x24 that asserts the '.setup-title' region is inside the step's visible region on first paint.
solution_review: Use focus(scroll_visible=False), then call_after_refresh(step.scroll_to_widget(target, animate=False)). That scroll is minimal and not centred, and it fixes 100x30 on its own. Do NOT 'always scroll Welcome home'. At 80x24 the content above the radio set is about 11 rows in a 10-row viewport, so scrolling home puts the focused control entirely below the fold, which fails WCAG 2.4.11. The solution's two rules contradict each other there. For 80x24, rely on the short tier or tighter Welcome copy. The pilot test should assert both the heading and the focused radio are inside the visible region.

cluster: Provider form is hand-coded rather than driven by a provider capability catalog
title: Setup handles one provider per run: env keys aren't marked in the list, and a key typed for another provider is silently dropped
problem: ProviderStep is single-select and commits one provider/model pair. Readiness the app already knows (env keys, stored keys, detected local servers) is shown only after a row is selected, never in the list, so a user with three exported keys must walk 60 rows to learn which are ready. Per-provider drafts survive switching in memory, but only the selected provider is committed, so a key typed for an earlier provider is discarded silently.
impact: Power user: three passes (or Settings detours) to configure providers the app already detected, about 75–90 keystrokes per Full pass. First-time user who tries two providers loses the first key without a word. Violates #7 Flexibility and efficiency of use, #6 Recognition rather than recall, #1 Visibility of system status, #5 Error prevention.
correction: The 'key typed for another provider is silently dropped' is not data loss. Per-provider drafts persist in memory (OrderedDict capped at 64, _MAX_PROVIDER_DRAFTS) and are restored when you re-select that provider. The provider+model commit happens at the Model step, so a key for A that was carried past Model IS saved to api_settings.A even if the user later goes back and picks B. The drop only affects a key typed and then abandoned on the Provider step by changing the single-select choice, and a single-select list does say 'one choice'. A user can still lose a key by arrowing in the list after typing it, because highlight equals select once the list has been interacted with. That accident-prone interaction is the real defect.

title: Provider checks behind a TLS-inspecting proxy fail with generic copy and no pointer to certificates or Settings ▸ Network
problem: The wizard's probe and discovery paths have no certificate-failure classification, so a TLS-inspection failure is reported like an outage or a bad key, with no route to the one setting that fixes it.
impact: Corporate first-time user abandons setup believing their key or the provider is broken. Violates #9 Help users recognize, diagnose and recover from errors.
correction: None for the core claim. Scope note: I drove the local (llama.cpp) path live. The cloud-provider path behind a real MITM proxy was not reproduced, but it reaches the same classifier: openai_compatible_model_discovery._transport_category maps every non-refused httpx.ConnectError, SSL verification failures included, to 'connection_error'. Wording differs by surface: 'could not reach the server' (Provider), 'isn't reachable … Start it' (Model, llama.cpp), 'Couldn't reach the server (connection_error)' (Model, other providers).

Utils/tls_trust.py: [network] ssl_verify accepts true/false/CA path; no OS trust-store (truststore) integration
tracked_task: none (TASK-24653 Done added `[network] ssl_verify`)
root_cause: Failure categories in the wizard cover refused/timeout/auth/content, not certificate verification.
solution: Classify connection errors whose cause is certificate verification into a “tls_untrusted” category. Copy: “Your network is intercepting secure connections (certificate not trusted). On a work network, add your company's CA in Settings ▸ Network, then Retry.” Button “Open Network settings” that returns to the wizard, or an inline “Trust this computer's certificate store” toggle writing network.ssl_verify.
solution_review: Classify certificate-verification failures in the shared discovery/probe module (an httpx.ConnectError whose cause chain contains ssl.SSLCertVerificationError) so every surface inherits it. Copy should say the server answered but its certificate isn't trusted, then point to Settings ▸ Network to add a CA bundle. Do not put an inline 'disable verification' or 'trust' toggle in the wizard: that nudges first-time users toward ssl_verify=false. The proposed 'Trust this computer's certificate store' toggle has no backing today (ssl_verify has no OS-store mode). A stronger long-term fix is to verify against the OS trust store via `truststore`, which fixes most corporate setups with zero UI.

title: After 'Enter skips', going Back shows the skipped provider's form; a key typed there is silently discarded and the step is skipped again
problem: Enter in the empty key field calls skip_without_key(), which clears selected_provider_key and _provider_choice_interacted but leaves OpenAI's Authentication form, key field and status on screen. When the user comes Back to add their key, the step looks exactly like 'OpenAI selected, paste key'. They paste a key and press Next, and commit() takes the skip path (_effective_provider_key returns '' because nothing is selected and the list was not touched). correction: The core claim reproduced exactly, live on a fresh profile at 120x40 (Quick track, OpenAI, Enter-skip, Ctrl+B, type key, Ctrl+N gives Step 3 'Pick a provider first — or type a model name below' with Provider '!'). One precision fix: _on_key_changed does more than clear the strip. It bumps the credential revision and shows 'Provider settings changed since test; test again.', but it never re-selects the provider. The key line is a visible tell the original missed. With a live selection the same keystrokes produce 'Key staged — it will be checked when you continue.' In the stale state the line keeps saying 'An API key is needed — paste it above. … No key yet? Enter skips this step' right under the pasted key. Newly observed: (1) Enter in the field with the key typed runs the probe and shows Console copy, 'Choose a provider and model before sending.', while OpenAI still looks selected. (2) Re-picking OpenAI in the list restores the selection but clears the typed key, so the user must paste it again. After a re-paste, Next stages normally ('Models for OpenAI.', Provider ✓). That control run shows the stale selection is the only fault. (3) In ANSI, the OpenAI row is styled byte-for-byte the same before and after the skip, so nothing on screen shows that the selection is gone. Not a duplicate. cross-cutting-06 has the same root, an invisible gap between highlight and selection (_effective_provider_key returns '' before interaction), and skip_without_key returns the step to exactly that pre-interaction state. new-a11y-terminal-visual-02 is the sibling consequence of the same incomplete reset in skip_without_key. provider-01 explains why skipping is a hidden Enter gesture in the first place. Cluster it with cross-cutting-06 / provider-01.
solution_review: Option (b), keeping the choice, is the right direction and (a) is wrong: resetting the step to blank on skip throws away the user's provider choice and turns Back into a dead end. Implement (b) as a one-shot skip, not a sticky 'skipped' flag. A sticky flag has to be cleared on typing, re-pick, Test, env-var detection and resume, and every missed event becomes this bug again. Instead, have the Enter-skip (and the explicit Skip control that provider-01 calls for) set a flag that commit() consumes for that single advance. skip_without_key should stop mutating selected_provider_key and _provider_choice_interacted at all. Back then shows an honest state: OpenAI selected, key empty, Next refusing as it does today, or staging the key if one is typed. Three companion fixes belong in the same change: (1) re-picking the already-shown provider must keep a typed draft key, not wipe it; (2) Model must take its provider context from what Provider committed or skipped, not from the live step (this also closes new-a11y-terminal-visual-02); (3) a deliberate skip should show as 'skipped' (–) on the tracker, not '!', which reads as an error. Keep the proposed regression test, skip → Back → type key → Next stages the key for openai and Model shows 'Models for OpenAI.', and add the re-pick-keeps-draft case.

title: Speech step reads [transcription] from a config key that does not exist at startup, so re-run prefill, the saved-language preselection and the GGUF status are always blank
problem: SpeechSetupStep reads app_instance.app_config['transcription'] (FRW:5453-5478, 5757-5759). The app's app_config is load_settings(), which has no top-level 'transcription' key; the raw section lives only under COMPREHENSIVE_CONFIG_RAW. So on any session that starts with [transcription] already set, the step never shows the 'Already your default: …' or 'Currently configured: <provider> — installing … will switch your default' line. It also preselects English/INT8 v2 even when German v3 is saved, reports 'No existing local transcribe.cpp GGUF configured.' when one is configured, and computes _use_as_default_offer from a blank prefill. The clobber warning (TASK-1301 AC#5's re-run prefill) is therefore dead in the live app. A user who re-runs setup and installs with the preselected English silently replaces their German default with no warning. The Summary is not affected, because it reads the raw TOML through load_cli_config_and_ensure_existence. Tests miss this because the fakes pass app_config={'transcription': {...}} at top level.

title: After an app restart, re-running setup shows every Tools gate OFF (and drops the saved splash card) because step prefill reads load_settings(), which omits [tools]
problem: ToolsStep and AppearanceStep prefill from wizard.app_instance.app_config. app.py:1124 sets that with load_settings(), a curated dict with no 'tools' section and no splash_screen.card_selection. On any re-run after a restart, read_wizard_prefill returns tool_gates=() and card_selection='', so every switch renders OFF even when gates are ON. tools_commit_delta compares against that same empty map. A gate shown OFF therefore cannot be turned off from the wizard (toggling on then off yields no delta). The Summary reloads the full TOML and contradicts the step: '✓ Tools — 2 enabled'. An explicit 'Surprise me' reset is also silently dropped after a restart (reset_to_random needs prefill.card_selection). In-session re-runs appear to work only because commit_config mirrors written sections into app_config. That is why earlier runs (power-user 85, cross-cutting-05) reported Tools as 'prefilled'.

correction: (1) The false verdict is not limited to 'not tested'. A successful Settings test shows 'Ready · verified HH:MM' for the blocked model, although that test 'lists models without generating', so 'verified' covers only the key and endpoint. (2) Code trace confirms the mechanism. ConsoleSettingsBlockerCode (Chat/console_session_settings.py:216-228) has no capacity code; its blockers are provider, endpoint, credential, model_missing, endpoint_unreachable and active_run only. build_console_settings_readiness (:1742-2004) sets operability='ready_to_send' whenever none of them applies, and readiness_words (:2713-2742) then prints Ready. (3) The switcher does show capacity ('~4k') but never links it to max_tokens 4096. The status bar says 'Context unknown' for the same model, so the two capacity surfaces also disagree with each other. (4) Readiness ignores send outcomes in general. On Gemini (gap-03 runs) the header still read 'Ready · not tested' after a 404 retired-model failure and after a 400 invalid-key failure. (5) Today only OpenAI is affected among shipped defaults. PROVIDER_CONTEXT_WINDOWS (Utils/token_counter.py:497-503) gives google 30720 against max_tokens 8192 and anthropic 200000; only openai's 4096 against 4096 leaves zero input capacity.
solution_review: The order is right: fix capacity at the source first. Better still, make the state impossible. Cap the response reservation whenever the window is only estimated (cross-cutting-01's review suggests min(max_tokens, window/4)), so an unknown model can never reach zero input capacity; the capacity facet then becomes defence in depth, not the main fix. Build the facet as a real blocker code (e.g. 'capacity_exhausted', recovery 'adjust_model_limits'). Compute it offline from resolve_context_window plus the configured max_tokens, the same inputs Console's send preflight uses, so the header, Settings, the switcher and the wizard Summary all derive from one verdict. Drop the proposed 'Ready · context size estimated': it labels a working state in jargon and would appear on every healthy '~' row. Speak only when capacity actually blocks, e.g. 'Not ready · replies fill the whole context', with a [Fix] that opens entry-exit-handoff-03's actions ([Set context size] [Shorten replies] [Switch model]). Two further changes the solution misses. First, rename the Settings test result to its real scope ('Key verified 00:56', not 'Ready · verified'), because it lists models and never generates. Second, let readiness downgrade on the current model's last send outcome (blocked, 401, 404), so the header never says Ready directly above a failed turn. Finally, unify 'Context unknown' (status bar) and '~4k' (switcher) into one estimated-window display. Cluster this with cross-cutting-01 (same root, wizard surface) and entry-exit-handoff-23 (the same verdict calls template placeholders Ready). cross-cutting-01 already cites the switcher capture and readiness_words as evidence, but its problem and solution cover only the Summary, so this is not a duplicate.

Every claim held: one Down hid the list, End selected 'vLLM (legacy alias)', Back from Model left focus on the off-screen list, and End then switched to 'vLLM (legacy alias)' again. Typing 'x' never reached the key field, which confirms the hidden list kept focus. The trigger is narrower than 'every arrow press'. Use a SetupCollapsible whose _on_collapsible_title_toggle sets a one-shot `_user_toggled` flag and whose _watch_collapsed scrolls only when it consumes that flag. Ctrl+N opened 'Continue anyway? / The server couldn't be reached, so this model setup is unverified.', and Continue gave 'Saving the provider and model setup failed.  Retry with Next, or go Back.' This repeated on all 3 attempts. Two precision fixes. (1) The cited mechanism 'commit_staged runs with nothing staged' is backwards: something IS staged. The skip path (skip_without_key, FRW:2952-2968, then ProviderStep.commit's early `return True, ""` at FRW:3249-3251) never releases the wizard-level _staged_provider_draft. (2) 'go Back' in the copy is not an escape: Back then Ctrl+N with no re-pick reproduces the loop, because Provider takes its skip path again. The loop needs a non-empty model ID. On fresh installs OpenAI gets the template prefill 'gpt-5.6-terra' ([model-04]), which is why OpenAI users hit it without typing anything. Confirmed escape: empty the field, then Ctrl+N and Continue anyway reaches 'Set up a voice' (Step 4) with Provider '!' and Model '!'. solution_review: Fix the source, not Model. The real defect is that 'skip the provider' clears ProviderStep's selection but not the wizard-level staged draft. The reset already exists: call clear_provider_setup_sensitive_state(clear_widgets=False) (FRW:8233) from the skip path, so Model honestly renders 'Pick a provider first'. Better still, fold it into one unselect_provider() that also resets the Authentication form, key field and status line, which fixes [new-provider-01] in the same change. Reject the proposal's alternative of making Model's commit treat 'nothing staged' as skip-safe. With the stale draft, Model still reads 'Models for OpenAI.' over 'gpt-5.6-terra', so a quiet success tells the user OpenAI/gpt-5.6-terra was saved when nothing was. That swaps a loud loop for a silent wrong outcome. Copy: when commit fails, name the cause and an action that works, e.g. 'No provider is connected, so there is no model to save. Go Back to connect one, or press Next to skip.' Never say 'server couldn't be reached' when nothing was selected. (1) Drop the new listing_requires_auth registry flag. The rule already exists as PUBLIC_MODEL_LISTING_PROVIDER_KEYS, and Settings and Console readiness already obey it. Move that set onto ProviderRecord as the single source, add huggingface and novita (both 200 on a bogus key), pin it with a test that probes nothing live, and make the wizard read it. One rule then gives one verdict on every surface.

(2) Keep the authenticated probes for OpenRouter (GET /api/v1/key, non-billable, and it returns the provider's own reason) and Hugging Face (GET huggingface.co/api/whoami-v2; note it's a different host from the router). Route both through the same discovery client and egress rules.

(3) Defer the consented 1-token completion for NVIDIA and Novita. In the wizard these presets can't list models at all today. Fix the chat-URL staging for all engine presets first (stage the base URL, as the control proves). Once they list, they join the public-listing set and get the same honest copy.

(4) Use the interim copy now, in the app's existing vocabulary rather than new words. Provider: 'OpenRouter lists models without checking keys — your key is checked when you send your first message.' Summary: '– Provider — openrouter (key not checked)', matching Settings' 'models listed; key not checked'. Never print 'it will be checked when you continue' for these providers.

(5) Success and failure copy: '✓ Key accepted by OpenRouter' / '✗ OpenRouter rejected this key: API key expired. Create a new one at openrouter.ai/keys.' is good. The provider's reason should come through gap-06's allowlisted error.message path, not ad-hoc parsing.

Core claim reproduced independently, and two parts are corrected.

Summary showed '✓ Provider — moonshot' and '✓ Default model — kimi-k3'.

The first send in the default saved chat produced '▸ Error · failed', expanding to '⚠ Provider continuation could not be persisted; retry or recover the interrupted run.' The docked panel read 'Response delivery status is unknown on the source device. Retry anyway may send a duplicate request because delivery status is unknown.' [Retry anyway] [Discard], and the composer read 'Send blocked — resolve response recovery first'. Discard clears the lock ('Response discarded.'), so this is not a permanent lock-out; every new saved-chat send repeats it.

2. 'The provider call succeeds' is now proven, not inferred from log timing. agent_runs.db records 'model_response_completed | completed | Model response completed' at 07:54:42.732Z, then the continuation error 5 ms later.

3. Correction: 'every reply is blocked' is true only for persistent chats. A Temporary chat with the same kimi-k3 replied 'vn4 temporary ok' after the capture gate's 'Send without capture'. The runtime's candidate invariants (agent_runtime.py:2192-2224) run in both modes, so they pass. The fault lies in the persistent branch.

4. Correction: 'persist_continuation then swallows the exception' is not established. The final-turn block has six distinct continuation_error() exits (agent_runtime.py:2197, 2204, 2220, 2224, 2232, 2235), and all of them emit the same summary; the swallowed persist exception (:1455) is only one of them. The store-level unit test for this exact path, test_reasoning_only_complete_continuation_uses_terminal_settlement (Tests/Chat/test_console_dispatch_continuation_handoff.py:685), passes ('1 passed'). So the store can settle a reasoning-only final checkpoint in isolation. The live defect is an integration precondition between the controller's dispatch-recovery state and the store, or the runtime's persistent-context check, that no current test drives.

No backlog task mentions 'continuation could not be persisted'.
solution_review:
Right priorities. Re-order them and sharpen one.

(a) Ship step 3 first and on its own: it is the user-facing fix. The app knows the reply arrived (the persisted 'Model response completed' step), so 'Response delivery status is unknown on the source device' and its duplicate-send warning are false here. When the optional reasoning-replay checkpoint can't be stored on a tool-free final turn, persist the reply as an ordinary assistant message without the continuation. Replay is 'accepted and never required' per model_capabilities.py:659-663. Show the text, record 'reasoning not preserved for replay' in the trace, and never mount the recovery panel or block the composer.

(b) Step 1 must be a Console pilot through the real controller and a saved conversation. A store-level test already exists for this path and passes, so another one would stay green while users stay blocked. Assert the Temporary-vs-saved difference directly.

(c) Step 2: beyond logging the store's RuntimeError, give each of the six continuation_error() exits its own non-secret reason code in the trace, so the next failure names its precondition.

(d) Step 4 is right. Put kimi-k3 in the provider smoke matrix behind cross-cutting-01's 'Ready to chat?' check. On the wizard side, that check is the only thing that would have turned this Summary ✓ into a truthful '✗ Can't chat yet'.

problem: The test used a bracketed paste. A key with a trailing U+200B (41 bullets for 40 characters) gives 'Something went wrong on this step, so setup stayed here. Retry with Next…', from a contained ValueError at first_run_setup_state.py:130; retrying can never succeed. A key in “…” smart quotes gets Provider ✓, then 'Couldn't reach the server (request failed). Check it's running', and back on Provider, 'The last connection check couldn't reach the server'. Control: the same fake key without quotes gives 'Authentication failed — this API key was rejected'. The field is masked with no reveal (#12), and resolve_provider_api_key only calls strip().
solution: Normalise pasted keys at the input: strip Cf/Zs/control characters, one pair of wrapping quotes, and a 'Bearer ' or 'NAME=' prefix. Say what was removed: 'Removed 1 invisible character and surrounding quotes from the pasted key.' Reject any remaining non-ASCII with a field-level message rather than a step crash. Map header-encoding errors to that message instead of 'couldn't reach the server'. Add Hypothesis tests and a pilot test that sends a Paste event.

title: Ctrl+Q quits setup instantly and skips the exit guard that Esc shows, while Ctrl+C's toast points users to it
problem: Esc with a staged key opens 'This provider connection is staged only in this wizard and has not been saved… [Keep going] [Exit setup]'. Ctrl+Q, the app-wide priority binding, exits at once (EXITED:0) and discards the key, because FirstRunSetupWizard has no confirm_quit (Settings, Chat, the profile interview and the Chunking Lab all have one). That contradicts ADR-031: 'Ctrl+Q never skips a guard Escape honours'. Ctrl+C shows Textual's stock toast 'Do you want to quit? Press ctrl+q to quit the app' over 'Next →' and 'Exit setup'. Repeats stack, and the toast teaches the very key that bypasses the guard.
solution: Add confirm_quit to FirstRunSetupWizard. It should reuse the exit dialog via await_quit_prompt ('Quit chatbook? Your OpenAI key hasn't been saved yet. Setup will resume at Provider next time.' [Keep setting up] [Quit]) and return True with no prompt when nothing is staged. Route ctrl+c to the same dialog, or replace the toast and de-duplicate it. Extend test_quit_flow_prompt_choke_point to cover screens that hold staged credentials.

title: First-reply failures after setup drop the provider's own reason and label stalls 'unexpected provider error'

title: A slow first local reply shows 90 s of unchanging 'Generating…', then fails with no elapsed time, cold-load allowance or guidance
problem: Ollama loads the model on the first request, and CPU prompt processing of a large model can take minutes. The wizard's '(recommended)' row can be a 70B model (#21). In the live run, 'Generating…' and 'Run: Agent running.' stayed unchanged from 5 s to 60 s. At 90 s the fixed DEFAULT_STALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS ended the run, and the header went back to 'Ready · not tested'. The only knob is a commented-out config key that no UI mentions.
solution: Give the first token a longer window (about 300 s for local providers, configurable) and keep 90 s for gaps between tokens. Show 'Waiting for llama.cpp to start answering… 0:42 — large local models can take a few minutes on the first message. [Stop]', and use Ollama /api/ps to report 'Loading <model>…'. On timeout, offer [Wait longer] [Try a smaller model] and name the setting. Don't reset the readiness pill to 'Ready' after a failed first reply.
